draft.title: Popular movements in America
card: Colonists who opposed British rule and, in time, backed independence. Not all colonists were Patriots, as Loyalists stayed loyal to Britain.
Groups that protested British measures. They organised boycotts of British goods, and some Sons of Liberty also used crowd action against officials.
Networks that shared news and plans by letter between towns and colonies. They helped colonists act together.
Colonial bodies that met outside the royal governors' control. They made decisions for the colony and took over its government.
draft.remember: Local protest groups, letter networks and new congresses turned scattered anger into organised action.

a.q: Which group's main job was to share news and plans between towns and colonies?
a.why: The Committees of Correspondence passed on news and plans by letter so that colonies could act together. The Sons of Liberty are the tempting choice, but they were known for protests and boycotts, not for running a letter network.
a.clue: Think about which group worked by writing letters.

b.q: In 1774 a colony's elected leaders meet without the royal governor's approval and begin making decisions for the colony. Which body does this describe?
b.why: A Provincial Congress met outside the governor's control and made decisions for the colony. A Committee of Correspondence is tempting, but it shared news between places and did not take over government.
b.clue: Which body took over running the colony rather than sharing news or protesting?
